content.content:
`deccy drafts` is one verb: invoked bare, it lists the registry's records and reports, for each record, whether the workspace the record names is missing while the record still says a draft is held there. The name is one lowercase word and everything after it is that verb's arguments, of which it declares none in v1 (wzmmmmsw); the purpose — listing the drafts the registry holds and reporting their drift — is served by this one verb and by no alias of it (znkxvuyv). Settling the word and the surface here is what the drift commitment left open: it fixed the reading and expressly deferred the verb name and the `drafts` surface, so this node names the verb and re-decides nothing about drift (vuopwuyo); `reconcile` names that reading in its prose and is not a second verb (znkxvuyv).

What the verb lists is exactly the registry's records, found by scanning `.deccy/work/` (twpvqstu). The set is the directory's contents: each record is one JSON document, its filename is the handle that keys it, and no index, edge or node names a record, so the only list there is is the one the directory gives (twpvqstu). Nothing outside that scan may appear in the listing — not a node, not an edit, not a draft the registry does not hold — and nothing inside it may be left out: landing deletes no record, the open and the landed documents sit in the same directory, and a scan taken after a landing still finds the landed one, so the listing includes every record the scan finds, landed ones included (twpvqstu, vkkwusty). A record appears once, under its handle, because the handle is its key; a node may be named by several records at once, and each of those is a record of its own and so a row of its own (owyntkvw).

For each record the listing reports the handle, the record's state, and the workspace the record carries by name and path (owyntkvw, vkkwusty). Those are references: the record names exactly one target node, one edit and one workspace, and none of them is the record's key, so the verb reports them as the record's references and never labels a row by a node or an edit, and never merges the several records that name one node (owyntkvw). The verb reads the registry, not the node space: a record is not the document `nodes/<id>.json`, is not listed with the nodes, is not validated as a node and carries no change, so the drafts listing is not a second node listing and cannot be produced by walking `nodes/`; a holder of a node, an edit or a workspace holds references, not the key, and cannot reach a record at all (owyntkvw).

Drift is decided per record by comparing the workspace reference the record carries against jj's workspaces. jj owns whether a workspace exists — a workspace is jj's object, and the record's naming of one is a reference rather than custody, since the registry creates no workspace for a record to name and removes none — so existence is jj's answer and the verb asks jj instead of inferring existence from the registry (vuopwuyo). An open record whose workspace jj does not have is drift: `open` is the record of a draft that has not landed, a draft is written in its own workspace, and the record therefore asserts a draft in a workspace that is gone (vuopwuyo). A landed record whose workspace is gone is not drift: the draft has landed, no draft is being written there any more, and the retained record outlives the workspace its draft used, so the absence is the normal end of the draft rather than a disagreement between the owners (vuopwuyo, vkkwusty). A workspace that jj still has for a landed record is not drift either: removing it would be the registry reaching into what jj owns, and its presence takes nothing from the record (vuopwuyo).

The open/landed split the drift test applies is the record's lifecycle, not a classification the verb invents. `open` and `landed` are the landing fact and its negation and exhaust the question whether the draft has landed, so the verb reads each value as that fact: `open` is tested for a missing workspace, `landed` is never drift and is never dropped from the listing, and no third category — stale, orphaned, unknown — is reported in their place (vkkwusty). Because `landed` is terminal and a redraft is a new record entering at `open`, drift is asked only of open records, and an earlier landed record is not reopened, re-tested or reported to make room for the redraft (vkkwusty).

The verb reads and only reads: it changes nothing — no node, no change, no marker, no record created, rewritten, dropped or forgotten — and a drifted record stays exactly as it stands, still open and still naming the workspace it names; the report is the whole of its effect (vuopwuyo). Repairing is excluded by that same stance and would also destroy what is reported: creating the missing workspace would make jj agree with the record from the outside, and deleting or rewriting the record would make the record agree with jj, and either way there would be no difference left to name; deleting a landed record is in any case what retention forbids, since the record is what the reversal of the recording that landed the draft is found through (vuopwuyo, vkkwusty). And because the verb mutates nothing, it is not an operation: it is never bracketed, leaves no marker and has nothing to undo (vuopwuyo).

What is checked is that the workspace exists, not what it contains. The disagreement this verb reports is between jj's ownership of existence and the registry's meaning of the record; whether a present workspace holds the changes the record's draft has made is a reading of jj's state in that workspace, not of the registry, and it is not drift as this verb reports it (vuopwuyo).

These clauses are one commitment, not several. The one name is what gives the purpose a verb (wzmmmmsw, znkxvuyv); the scan is what fixes which drafts appear (twpvqstu); the record's references and non-node identity are what each row may say and why the listing is not the node listing (owyntkvw); the open/landed fact is what makes an absence drift or not (vuopwuyo, vkkwusty); and the read-only stance is why the report can be the whole answer rather than a repair (vuopwuyo). Change the name and the purpose has no verb; list from the nodes and the records disappear; drop the landed records and the scan stops being complete; widen the drift test and every landed record's empty workspace becomes a false alarm; repair instead of report and there is no report left. They answer one question — how a caller sees the drafts the registry holds and which of them have lost their workspace — with one answer: `deccy drafts`, reading the registry and jj, listing every record and reporting only the open ones whose workspace is gone.

Deliberately not here: the output's line form, exit status and help text, and whether a clean report and a drifted one are distinguished by status; which jj invocation the verb uses to ask for jj's workspaces, and how it matches a record's workspace name and path to one; whether the verb ever takes arguments and how a caller asks for one state rather than another, which the registry commitment left open (twpvqstu); how a workspace is created or removed, since the verb neither does nor repairs either (vuopwuyo); what an operator does with a report (vuopwuyo); and how a record's fields are written or versioned (owyntkvw). Each of those can be decided, changed or dropped without touching what is settled here.
content.rationale:
The surface exists because the drift commitment left it unbuilt: drift is a difference the registry and jj can hold, reconcile reports it and repairs nothing, and the verb name and the `drafts` surface were expressly deferred to a separate commitment (vuopwuyo). This node is that commitment and nothing else: it fixes one verb, its list and its report. The name follows the invocation shape — one verb per invocation, a single lowercase word, everything after it the verb's arguments — so the surface is one word that declares no arguments in v1 (wzmmmmsw); it follows one verb per purpose with no aliases, so listing the registry and reporting drift is served by exactly `drafts` and `reconcile` is not a second spelling of it (znkxvuyv); and it decides nothing about what drift is, because that was already decided (vuopwuyo).

The listing set is the registry's storage rule read from the listing side. Records are one JSON document per handle under `.deccy/work/`, the filename is the handle, they are found by scanning the directory, and landed records remain (twpvqstu). That makes the list the directory's contents: a verb listing nodes or edits would be reporting keys the registry does not have, and a verb that hid landed records would be treating landing as a deletion that retention does not permit (twpvqstu, vkkwusty). That the handle is the only key and that node, edit and workspace are references (owyntkvw) is what fixes each row: one row per handle, with the references reported rather than used as keys. That a record is not a node document (owyntkvw) is why the drafts listing reads `.deccy/work/` and not `nodes/`, and why it adds no field to the graph.

The drift test is the drift commitment applied to a verb rather than a test of the verb's own. jj owns workspace existence and the registry owns meaning, so the comparison is the record's workspace reference against what jj has (vuopwuyo); `open` asserts a draft being written there, so a missing workspace is drift, while `landed` asserts no such thing, so the same absence is the normal end of the draft, and retention is why that end is not a deletion (vuopwuyo, vkkwusty). The two values being the landing fact and its negation is why the test reads them as that fact and reports no third category (vkkwusty).

The read-only stance is not a caution added on top; it is what makes the output a report. Reconcile changes nothing, repairs nothing and drops nothing, and a drifted record stays open and still names the missing workspace (vuopwuyo); a landed record is likewise never dropped, since it is what a reversal of the landing finds the draft through (vkkwusty). Because the verb mutates nothing it is not an operation, leaves no marker and has nothing to undo (vuopwuyo).

What is left out is left to its owners: output form and exit status, the jj invocation used to read workspaces, and arguments or per-state filtering (twpvqstu); workspace creation and removal, and what an operator does with a report (vuopwuyo); and the record's written field set and version (owyntkvw).
